name: Grade-School Math with Irrelevant Context (GSM-IC)
description: GSM-IC is an arithmetic reasoning dataset designed to measure the distractibility of large language models by including irrelevant information in problem descriptions. It evaluates how irrelevant context affects model problem-solving accuracy and the effectiveness of mitigation strategies.
reputation: A well-known robustness benchmark in arithmetic reasoning, commonly used to test LLM distractibility and mitigation methods.
notes: Focuses on the impact of irrelevant context on arithmetic reasoning performance and explores mitigation techniques such as self-consistency decoding and prompt instructions.
